Can robot agents think fast enough?

A benchmark for language-model agents controlling a simulated robot on long-horizon household tasks, where the world keeps moving while the model thinks. Every decision costs time, objects get displaced, and the scene changes under the agent's feet.

What the benchmark asks

Embodied planning benchmarks freeze the world while a model thinks, so they cannot tell whether a planner is fast enough for a robot. Here model calls overlap with execution and thinking time is charged to the task. Each question below names its method, the result so far, and the cases that show it. More runs are in progress, so these results may change.

Tasks

Two tracks. The visual reasoning track (8 tasks) is the main result: objects must be found in the image. The state track has 60 task configurations in six categories, built on the RoboCerebra scenes (LIBERO / robosuite, MuJoCo, 20 Hz control). They come from 30 base tasks: Observation Mismatch and Random Disturbance rerun the ten Ideal tasks under new conditions, and Mix reruns ten Memory tasks with both conditions on. A task is a list of ordered subgoals, such as "pick up the butter" and "butter in the drawer". The score is the fraction completed within 300 s, leaving out subgoals already done at the start. The reference is a scripted executor following the demonstration plan, with no language model.

Closed decision models (via OpenRouter)

Listed separately and not ranked with the open models, because their clock differs: token clocks fitted to the API latencies (0.6–2.4 s of overhead per call), and the API does not report prefix-cache hits, so caching cannot be credited. Jev-1.14 and GPT-6 Luna in decision mode are fast branches; GPT-6 Luna is the slow branch. GPT-6 Luna's text replies are sometimes blocked by OpenAI's policy filter (about 2.5% of calls on the state track and 11% on the visual track); calls still blocked after one retry count as invalid replies. Same track and time budget as above.

When a slow branch helps

A slow branch can only fix decisions the fast branch gets wrong, and only if its answer arrives in time. To separate the two, the slow branch is replaced by an oracle that publishes the remaining steps of the reference plan after a fixed latency L (state track, token clock at k = 1, one seed). The gain is the score difference to Fast · Jev with the same fast model, with 95% bootstrap intervals over task goals.

Jev confidence is a weak failure signal

Fixing late advice and stale plans

Wait for the advice after a failed skill (wall clock)

Dual · Advice with the fast branch held for up to 3 s after a failure until the advice triggered by that failure arrives, paired with the original runs on the same tasks and seeds (60 tasks × 3 seeds). Δ is the paired score difference with a bootstrap 95% interval and a sign-flip test p-value.

Re-plan only after the state changes (paused clock)

Dual · Plan under the paused clock: when a plan is discarded, the original coordinator re-plans at once from the same frozen snapshot, which can repeat the same discarded plan dozens of times. The variant waits until the next skill finishes (or 5 s of environment time) before re-planning. Pilot tasks, seed 1.

How it works

The simulator runs in real time. The agent reads timestamped snapshots, issues skill calls to a scripted executor, and can cancel them at any control step. Nothing waits for the model.

Environment

  • MuJoCo physics at 20 Hz; the agent sees object states and a 3rd-person camera image.
  • Skills: pick, place, place-on, pour, open / close drawer, turn on; each runs for seconds and can be interrupted.
  • Dynamics from RoboCerebra: random disturbances, observation mismatch, hidden objects in drawers.

Agent frameworks

    Clocks and metrics

    • Wall (default): the world advances during inference by the measured latency; results reflect decisions and serving speed. Hardware is reported per row.
    • Token: the world pauses during the call, then advances by a fixed cost: . Independent of hardware; rewards short outputs and cache reuse.
    • Paused: inference costs no environment time — an upper bound on decision quality.
    • Score: fraction of subgoals completed (± SD over 3 seeds). Success: whole task completed. pass^3: task completed in all 3 seeds.
